$comment: Ground truth for target/. Holes are seeded on purpose; controls are done correctly and are there to catch false positives. Paths are relative to target/.

holes.summary: public.audit_log has RLS off, so anyone with the anon key can read and write it.
public.feature_flags has RLS on and no policies: deny-all for the API, so the client's flag read silently returns nothing.
public.messages has a select policy using (true): every direct message is readable by anyone, signed in or not.
public.profiles update policy has no WITH CHECK and no column limit, so a user can set their own plan to 'pro' without paying.
public.get_message_stats() is SECURITY DEFINER with no fixed search_path.
public.recent_notes is a view over the private notes table without security_invoker, so it returns every user's note titles.
The invoices storage bucket is public and has a select policy that lets anyone list every invoice.
A "use client" component builds a Supabase client with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.
The Stripe secret key is read from NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, which Next.js inlines into the browser bundle.
The Stripe webhook route parses the body as an event without checking the stripe-signature header, then upgrades the plan.
public.user_directory selects id and email from auth.users and is granted to anon: every user's email is public.
public.admin_set_plan() is SECURITY DEFINER, has no caller check and is granted to anon: anyone can change anyone's plan over RPC.

controls.summary: public.notes: RLS on, owner-scoped policies for all four commands, WITH CHECK on writes.
public.note_counts: a view with security_invoker = true.
public.handle_new_user(): SECURITY DEFINER trigger function with search_path = '' and EXECUTE revoked from the API roles.
The avatars bucket: private, read and upload limited to the user's own folder.
A "use client" component that uses only the public anon key.
The service role client, in a server-only module.
A route handler that checks the signed-in user before creating a Checkout session.
